== Side event pages (October 2026) ==
=== Build notes ===
* Pages for Iron Man, No Such Thing As Luck, Players Choice, Japanese Sealed Deck and the Gauntlet built from Decipher's DecipherCon 1999 event-score pages (calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/SWnn_n.html, Wayback 2000–2001). Score = match points (differential).
=== Missing data ===
* Not built: Allegiances (two 4-player tables, no overall winner), the second "SW Iron Man" sheet (SW11_2), Progressive Sealed (two differing sheets SW22_1/SW22_2), the Gauntlet game-1 sheet (SW30_2). Exact day of each side event is not on the score pages (Iron Man was Friday per Lalumiere). [[User:Datacard Grok|Datacard Grok]] ([[User talk:Datacard Grok|talk]]) 21:57, 13 October 2026 (UTC)

== Style pass (2026-10-15) ==
=== Missing data ===
* Side events table: winners of Allegiances, SW Iron Man and Progressive Sealed Deck were "Unknown"; now blank.
=== Possibly faulty data ===
* Team Event: this page (Torch Industries Drazin deck page) lists [[Paul Todd Feldman]], [[Maarten Logghe]], [[Bastian Winkelhaus]] and one unknown player. The Trandosite profile on [[Martin Akesson]] (31 August 2000) says Akesson won the DecipherCon '99 team tournament with Paul Feldman, Koen Meijsen and Yannick LaPointe.
=== Marginal cuts ===
* Venue bullets (repeated the lead): "Dates: 11–14 November 1999 (Thursday–Sunday)"; "Site: Cavalier Hotel / Cavalier Hotel at the Oceanfront, Virginia Beach, Virginia".
* Captions were: "Tournament hall, chandelier ballroom with ocean view"; "Staff tables with ocean view through arched windows" (Kevin Reitzel Facebook collection).

== Team Event winners (2026-10-16) ==
Article now lists [[Martin Akesson]], [[Paul Todd Feldman]], [[Koen Meijssen]] and [[Yannick Lapointe]], from the Trandosite Akesson interview of 31 August 2000. Feldman's March 2000 Torch Industries deck pages confirm he was on the winning team. The 2025 DRTORCH interview auto-captions ("Martin Logan", "Bastion", fourth forgotten) stay on [[Talk:DecipherCon 1999 Team Event]].
